status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Read the real Ethiopian translation text directly (Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/acts_64.json, all 28 chapters spot-verified plus a full-file name-occurrence sweep across every character/place name appearing in the already-completed KJV Character Index for this book). Content is verbatim-identical to the KJV Acts already indexed in this project (same Peter-then-Paul two-act structure, same 28 chapters/1007 verses, same wording on every spot-checked passage including Judas's field-purchase death in 1:18-19, Ananias/Sapphira in 5:1-10, Herod Agrippa I 'eaten of worms' in 12:20-23, and Agrippa II's 'almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian' in 26:28) - this Ethiopian translation shows none of the real structural/content divergences found elsewhere in this same source (e.g. its own distinct 1 Esdras-tradition Ezra). Structure is therefore adapted directly from the validated KJV Acts index (same tier count/shape, same manager promotions, same naming-collision flags and submanager assignments) rather than re-derived from scratch, per the task's own guidance for content-identical shared-canon books - every verse reference and character detail was re-verified against this translation's own extracted text, not copied blind. All ids are suffixed '_ethiopian' to keep this translation's roster namespace-isolated from the KJV set. No law/theme tiers, matching the KJV finding that Acts has no detached instructional sections - even the long speeches (Pentecost sermon, Stephen's defense, Paul's Areopagus speech) are personally-embodied moments logged as verse entries under their speaker. No standalone Jesus tier (he ascends in Acts 1 before the narrative proper begins); his one appearance to Saul on the Damascus road (9:3-9) is logged as a verse entry on Paul's tier. Naming collisions carried over unchanged, since the underlying names/events are identical: four men named Herod across Acts+Matthew's scope; three-to-four men named Simon; two James beyond the apostle-roster-only James son of Alphaeus; three men named Ananias; three men named Judas; the Ephesus-riot 'Gaius of Macedonia' vs. the travel-roster 'Gaius of Derbe' naming variance (kept unresolved in genealogyLists, not merged). Silas and Herod Agrippa II remain independently promoted past mere-companion status for the same reasons as the KJV draft (Silas's own personally-embodied Philippi ordeal; Agrippa II's two full chapters of personal judgment of Paul's case); Ananias of Damascus remains a submanager rather than a promoted manager, for the same single-episode-serving-Paul's-arc reasoning.

characters.name: Simon Peter

verses.note: Leads the church in choosing Matthias to replace Judas among the twelve.
Preaches at Pentecost; about three thousand souls added that day.
Heals a man lame from birth at the temple's Beautiful gate, with John.
Arrested with John, testifies before the council, 'we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.'
Confronts Ananias and Sapphira over their lie to the Holy Ghost; both die.
Imprisoned with the apostles, freed by an angel, testifies before the council again.
Heals Aeneas at Lydda; raises Dorcas from the dead at Joppa; lodges with Simon a tanner.
Sees the vision of the sheet with unclean animals; preaches to Cornelius's household as the Holy Ghost falls on Gentiles.
Imprisoned by Herod, freed by an angel, comes to Mary's house where Rhoda answers the door.
Speaks at the Jerusalem council, affirming salvation by grace for Gentile believers.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: lodges with 'Simon a tanner' (9:43, 10:6), a different man from Simon the sorcerer under Philip's tier; folded into Peter's own verses since he takes no independent action.
Text verified identical to KJV on every spot-checked passage, including verse numbering.

characters.name: John (son of Zebedee)

genealogy.father: zebedee — Matthew 4:21, not individually indexed in Acts

verses.note: Goes to the temple with Peter; present at the healing of the lame man.
Arrested and examined alongside Peter before the council.
Sent with Peter to Samaria; lays hands on believers to receive the Holy Ghost.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: distinct from John Mark (Barnabas's tier) and from the unnamed high-priestly-kindred 'John' at 4:6 (kept in genealogyLists).

verses.note: Put forward alongside Joseph called Barsabas; chosen by lot to replace Judas among the eleven.

characters.name: Mary, the mother of John Mark

verses.note: Her house is where 'many were gathered together praying' the night the angel frees Peter.

characters.name: Ananias and Sapphira

spouses: each other, a married couple — Acts 5:1

verses.note: Ananias sells land, keeps back part of the price, lies to Peter about it, and dies.
Sapphira, unaware, repeats the same lie about the price and dies as well.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: distinct from Ananias of Damascus and Ananias the high priest, both indexed under Paul's tier below.

verses.note: A Pharisee and doctor of the law, advises the council to leave the apostles alone, citing Theudas and Judas of Galilee as precedent.
A damsel who answers the gate when Peter knocks; too glad to open it, she runs to report he's there instead.

characters.name: Dorcas (Tabitha)

verses.note: A disciple at Joppa 'full of good works and almsdeeds'; dies, mourned by widows showing coats she made, raised by Peter.

funFacts: Her name is given in both Aramaic (Tabitha) and Greek (Dorcas) by the text itself.

characters.name: Simon called Zelotes

verses.note: Named among the eleven remaining apostles gathered in the upper room; no further individual action.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: distinct from Simon Peter, Simon the sorcerer, and Simon the tanner.

characters.name: Stephen

verses.note: Chosen as one of the seven to serve, 'full of faith and of the Holy Ghost.'
Does great wonders among the people; opponents unable to resist his wisdom.
Falsely accused of blasphemy before the council; his face seen 'as it had been the face of an angel.'
Delivers his defense, retelling Israel's history from Abraham through Solomon.
Stoned to death; sees the heavens opened and the Son of man at God's right hand; prays for his killers as Saul looks on.

funFacts: The first Christian martyr recorded in scripture; his death provokes the great persecution that scatters the church (8:1).

characters.name: Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas

verses.note: Named alongside Stephen and Philip as the seven chosen to serve tables; Nicolas specified as 'a proselyte of Antioch.'

characters.name: Philip the Evangelist

children: four unnamed daughters, virgins, which did prophesy — Acts 21:9, not individually indexed

verses.note: Chosen as one of the seven deacons.
Preaches Christ in a city of Samaria; great joy results as unclean spirits and the sick are healed.
Simon the sorcerer believes his preaching and is baptized.
Led by an angel to the Gaza road; explains Isaiah's prophecy to an Ethiopian eunuch and baptizes him.
Caught away by the Spirit, found preaching from Azotus onward to Caesarea.
Now called 'Philip the evangelist,' hosts Paul at Caesarea; his four daughters prophesy.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: distinct from Philip the Apostle, listed only in the roster of the twelve (1:13) with no further action.

Note: this book's own Ethiopian-translation text records this scene of Philip and an Ethiopian eunuch directly (8:26-39) — a real, notable point of resonance with the translation itself, though the text of the passage is identical to the KJV account, not altered or expanded.

verses.note: Had bewitched Samaria with sorcery, claiming to be 'some great one'; believes Philip's preaching and is baptized.
Offers Peter and John money to buy the power to bestow the Holy Ghost; is sharply rebuked and asks for prayer.

characters.name: The Ethiopian Eunuch

verses.note: A man of Ethiopia, an officer of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, returning from worship at Jerusalem, reading Isaiah.
Asks Philip who the prophet means, is taught of Jesus, requests baptism, and goes on his way rejoicing.

funFacts: Left deliberately unnamed by the text itself in every translation checked, including this one; no name is asserted here.

characters.name: Barnabas

verses.note: A Levite of Cyprus named Joses, sells land and lays the money at the apostles' feet; surnamed Barnabas, 'son of consolation.'
Takes the newly-converted Saul and brings him to the apostles, vouching for him.
Sent to Antioch, exhorts the believers there, 'a good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.'
Goes to Tarsus to fetch Saul; together they teach at Antioch for a year.
Set apart with Saul for missionary work by the Holy Ghost.
Mistaken for the god Jupiter by the crowd at Lystra.
Attends the Jerusalem council; later has sharp contention with Paul over John Mark and sails for Cyprus with Mark instead.

funFacts: His original name, Joses, is stated directly by the text (4:36).

verses.note: His mother Mary's house is the prayer meeting Peter comes to; taken along by Barnabas and Saul from Jerusalem.
Attends Paul and Barnabas as their minister on Cyprus, then departs at Perga to return to Jerusalem.
Paul refuses to take him on the second journey; the disagreement causes Paul and Barnabas to part ways.

characters.name: Saul / Paul the Apostle

verses.note: As Saul, keeps the clothes of Stephen's executioners and makes havoc of the church, dragging believers to prison.
Blinded by a light on the road to Damascus; hears the risen Christ's voice, 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?'
Ananias of Damascus restores his sight and he is baptized.
First called by the name 'Paul': 'Saul, (who also is called Paul).'
First missionary journey with Barnabas through Cyprus and Asia Minor.
Sees the vision of a man of Macedonia calling him over.
Preaches to the philosophers at the Areopagus in Athens on 'the unknown god.'
Seized in the temple at Jerusalem; a riot breaks out and he is arrested.
Shipwrecked en route to Rome after appealing to Caesar.
Bitten by a viper on Malta and shakes it off unharmed.
Spends two years in his own hired house in Rome, preaching with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

funFacts: Acts 22:3 states he was born in Tarsus in Cilicia; 23:6 that he was 'a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee'; 22:28 that he was 'free born,' a Roman citizen by birth.

characters.name: Ananias of Damascus

verses.note: A disciple at Damascus, initially fearful, told in a vision to go to Saul.
Lays hands on Saul, restoring his sight; Saul is baptized and receives food.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: distinct from Ananias the husband of Sapphira (Peter's tier) and Ananias the high priest, indexed below.
Not promoted to a full manager tier — his action, however vivid, is confined to a single episode serving Paul's own arc, unlike Cornelius or Apollos.

verses.note: A disciple at Lystra, son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father; Paul has him circumcised and takes him along.
Sent ahead with Silas while Paul goes to Athens.
Listed among Paul's traveling companions from Macedonia to Asia.
Paul finds them at Corinth, recently come from Italy after Claudius commanded Jews to leave Rome; lodges and works with them as tentmakers.
Sail with Paul to Syria; left at Ephesus.
Hear Apollos speak boldly in the synagogue and take him aside to expound the way of God more perfectly.
A Jewish sorcerer and false prophet on Cyprus who withstands Paul and Barnabas, seeking to turn the proconsul from the faith; Paul strikes him blind.
The deputy (proconsul) of Cyprus, 'a prudent man,' desires to hear the word of God and believes after seeing Elymas struck blind.
A silversmith who makes shrines for Diana of the Ephesians; incites fellow craftsmen against Paul's preaching, fearing loss of trade.
The resulting uproar fills the city's theatre until the townclerk quiets the crowd.
A young man who falls asleep during Paul's long sermon at Troas, falls from a third-story window and is taken up dead; Paul restores him alive.
The 'chief man of the island' of Malta, lodges the shipwrecked party three days; his father is healed by Paul.
Other diseased islanders come and are healed; the party is honored with many gifts.
A centurion of Augustus's band charged with delivering Paul to Rome; courteously lets him visit friends at Sidon.
Prevents the soldiers from killing the prisoners during the shipwreck, 'willing to save Paul.'

characters.name: Felix

verses.note: The governor before whom the high priest Ananias and the orator Tertullus accuse Paul; Paul answers for himself.
Sends for Paul with his wife Drusilla to hear him on faith in Christ; trembles but hopes for a bribe and leaves Paul bound two years.

funFacts: Drusilla is named as 'his wife, which was a Jewess' but takes no independent action, so is not given her own entry.

verses.note: Succeeds Felix as governor; before him Paul appeals to Caesar rather than be tried at Jerusalem.
Lays Paul's case before the visiting Herod Agrippa II, unsure what charge to send with him to Rome.
Deputy of Achaia; dismisses the Jews' accusation against Paul as a matter of their own law, and 'cared for none of those things' when Sosthenes is beaten before his judgment seat.
A prophet who signifies by the Spirit a great dearth throughout the world, which comes to pass in Claudius's day.
Takes Paul's girdle, binds his own hands and feet, and prophesies Paul will be bound at Jerusalem.
A seller of purple of Thyatira, a worshipper of God at Philippi; the Lord opens her heart, she and her household are baptized.
Paul and Silas return to her house after their release from prison.
Listed among Paul's traveling companions, identified as 'of Asia.'
Jews from Asia wrongly suppose Paul brought him into the temple — the accusation that sparks the riot leading to Paul's arrest.

characters.name: Aristarchus

verses.note: A Macedonian, Paul's companion in travel, seized alongside Gaius and dragged into the Ephesus theatre during the riot.
Listed among Paul's company into Asia, identified as one 'of the Thessalonians.'
Boards the ship to Rome with Paul, 'a Macedonian of Thessalonica.'

funFacts: Present with Paul across three separate scenes spanning roughly a decade of narrative time.

characters.name: Ananias the High Priest

verses.note: Presiding as high priest at Paul's hearing, commands those standing by to smite him on the mouth; Paul rebukes him, then apologizes on learning he is the high priest.
Comes to Caesarea with the elders and the orator Tertullus to formally accuse Paul before Felix.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: a third distinct Ananias in this book, separate from Ananias of Damascus and Ananias husband of Sapphira.

verses.note: A centurion of the Italian band at Caesarea, devout, feared God with all his house, gave much alms, prayed always; an angel tells him to send for Peter.
Awaits Peter with his kinsmen and near friends gathered together.
The Holy Ghost falls on him and his household as Peter speaks; they are baptized, the first recorded Gentile converts.
His conversion is defended by Peter before the Jerusalem church as evidence God grants repentance unto life to the Gentiles also.

characters.name: Herod (Agrippa I)

verses.note: Stretches forth his hand to vex certain of the church, and kills James (brother of John) with the sword.
Imprisons Peter also, intending to bring him forth after Easter; an angel frees Peter instead.
Gives a public oration; the people cry 'It is the voice of a god, and not of a man'; an angel of the Lord smites him because he gave not God the glory, and he is eaten of worms and dies.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: called simply 'Herod' throughout chapter 12 — one of four men named Herod across this book+Matthew's scope.

characters.name: James (son of Zebedee)

genealogy.father: zebedee — Matthew 4:21, not individually indexed in Acts

verses.note: Killed with the sword by Herod Agrippa I — his death is reported in a single verse.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: distinct from James of Jerusalem and James son of Alphaeus (apostle roster only, 1:13).

verses.note: Peter, freed from prison, instructs the disciples to 'shew these things unto James, and to the brethren.'
Presides at the Jerusalem council, rendering judgment that Gentile believers not be troubled with circumcision.
Paul reports to James and the elders at Jerusalem; they advise him to join four men under a vow.
A Jew born at Alexandria, eloquent, mighty in the scriptures, knowing only the baptism of John; Priscilla and Aquila expound the way of God to him more perfectly.
Helps the believers in Achaia much, mightily convincing the Jews publicly that Jesus was Christ.
Paul arrives at Ephesus while Apollos is at Corinth.
A chief man among the brethren, a prophet, sent with Judas Barsabas to carry the Jerusalem council's letter to Antioch.
Chosen by Paul to accompany him on the second missionary journey after the split with Barnabas.
Beaten with many stripes and cast into prison at Philippi alongside Paul.
Sings praises with Paul at midnight; an earthquake opens the prison doors and the jailor is converted.
Paul declares them both Roman citizens, uncondemned and beaten publicly.
Travels with Paul through Thessalonica and Berea.
Rejoins Paul at Corinth, coming from Macedonia.

characters.name: Judas surnamed Barsabas

verses.note: Chosen with Silas, chief men among the brethren, to carry the Jerusalem council's letter to Antioch and exhort the brethren, being prophets themselves.
Sent away in peace back to the apostles after his work at Antioch is done.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: distinct from Judas Iscariot and from the Judas of Damascus address marker (9:11).

characters.name: The Philippian Jailor

verses.note: Wakes to find the prison doors open after the earthquake and draws his sword to kill himself, until Paul cries out that all are present.
Asks 'what must I do to be saved,' believes on the Lord Jesus Christ, washes their stripes, and is baptized with his whole household.

funFacts: Left unnamed by the text — called only 'the keeper of the prison.'

characters.name: Herod Agrippa II

verses.note: Arrives at Caesarea with Bernice to salute Festus; hears the perplexing case against Paul and says, 'I would also hear the man myself.'
Paul is brought before him and Bernice 'with great pomp,' so Festus can have a charge to send with him to Rome.
Gives Paul leave to speak for himself and hears his full defense and testimony of the risen Christ.
Replies, 'Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.'
Rises with Festus and Bernice, privately concludes Paul 'might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.'

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: son of Herod Agrippa I; one of four men named Herod across this book+Matthew's scope.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list because Acts does not differentiate their individual actions, or because a link to another named figure is genuinely uncertain from the text alone. Carried over from the validated KJV Acts index since this translation's own text is verbatim-identical on every checked passage.

sanhedrinMembers4_6.note: Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest — present at Peter and John's hearing but given no individual action; this 'John' is a third distinct figure from John son of Zebedee and John Mark.

theudasAndJudasOfGalilee.note: Two failed revolutionary leaders cited by Gamaliel as historical precedent — reported speech about the past, not acting characters.

antiochProphetsAndTeachers.note: Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen (brought up with Herod the tetrarch) — named alongside Barnabas and Saul, no further individual action.

sonsOfSceva.note: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, attempt to exorcise a spirit by Paul's name and are overpowered; not individually named.

alexanderOfEphesusRiot.note: A Jew put forward by the crowd during the Ephesus riot, shouted down before he can speak — likely distinct from the Alexander named at 4:6.

tertullus.note: A professional orator hired to present the accusation against Paul before Felix — a one-scene legal figure.

sosthenes.note: Ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, beaten before Gallio's judgment seat; possibly but not confirmed the same Sosthenes of 1 Corinthians 1:1.

egyptianOf21_38.note: An unnamed Egyptian rebel leader the chief captain mistakes Paul for — a passing historical reference.

act20TravelCompanions.note: 'Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.' Timothy, Trophimus, and Aristarchus indexed individually above; Sopater, Secundus, Gaius, and Tychicus kept as one collective entry.

gaiusNamingVariance.note: 'Gaius... of Macedonia' (19:29) and 'Gaius of Derbe' (20:4) carry different location descriptors — possibly two different men; flagged as unresolved, not merged.

judasOfDamascus.note: 'The street which is called Straight... the house of Judas' — a pure address marker, not an acting character.

judasIscariotDeathActs.note: Peter recounts Judas's betrayal and death, described here as falling headlong and bursting asunder in a field bought with the reward of iniquity — the same physical detail as this translation's own text, logged descriptively without reconciling against Matthew 27:5's differing account.
